condition_trigger: Garment front zipper extends partially from collar to chest only and does NOT open down to hem.
rule_instruction: Classify garment_type as "Half-Zip Pullover" (半拉鏈套頭衫). Distinct from full-zip jackets and crew pullovers.
example_positive: Half-Zip Pullover with stand collar and chin guard
example_negative: Do NOT classify as Jacket, Coat, or Cardigan

rule_title: Do NOT Classify Partial Zip as Jacket
condition_trigger: Front zipper terminates at upper or mid-chest.
rule_instruction: Negative Rule: Never classify a garment with a partial neck/chest zip as "Jacket". Jackets must feature a full-length separable zipper opening entirely from neck to bottom hem.

condition_trigger: Tag or spec mentions S.Cafe or PU.
rule_instruction: Extract "S.Cafe coffee yarn" with anti-odour and anti-bacteria functional properties. Extract "PU" as "PU (Polyurethane / 聚氨酯)".
example_negative: Generic "Polyester Blend" omitting S.Cafe or PU

rule_title: Strip Internal Fabric Code (F-xxx) from Buyer Fabric
condition_trigger: Fabric spec contains Winzen internal prefix "F-xxx" (e.g. F-670, F-760).
rule_instruction: Negative Rule: Do NOT include internal factory fabric tracking codes in buyer-facing fabric fields. Strip "F-xxx" automatically.
example_negative: F-670 88% S.CAFE PES 12% PU (Internal code must be removed)

condition_trigger: Fabric weight is indicated or requested in pounds per dozen (LBS/DOZ).
rule_instruction: Negative Rule: Never record fabric weight in LBS/DOZ (obsolete imperial metric). Always convert to or enforce standard "gm/m2" (GSM).

rule_title: Do NOT Confuse Rubber Print with Embroidery
condition_trigger: Chest or sleeve artwork has smooth, flexible, or glossy raised surface without visible thread stitches.
rule_instruction: Negative Rule: Do NOT identify smooth, continuous graphic artwork as embroidery. Label explicitly as "Rubber Print" (膠印) unless thread stitching is visually confirmed.
example_positive: Chest rubber print graphic with micro-ventilation punch holes
example_negative: Chest embroidery (INCORRECT when no thread stitches exist)

condition_trigger: Garment exhibits screen/rubber printing, contrast edge piping, or waistband drawstrings.
rule_instruction: Automatically append standardized tags: #print, #piping, and #waistband_drawstring for quick multi-sample searching.

condition_trigger: Buyer code has BG, BB, or BO followed by M (Men) or W (Women).
rule_instruction: Decompose code: BGM = Boss Green Men (Golf/Sport), BBM = Boss Black Men (Tailored), BOM = Boss Orange Men (Casual/Denim). Note Hugo = youthful trendy line vs Boss = core mature line.

condition_trigger: Garment exhibits tie-dye, dip-dye, or washed swirl coloring.
rule_instruction: Evaluate visual saturation. If color penetration is deep, saturated, and uniform across yarns, designate primary as Reactive Tie-Dye (#reactive_tie_dye). If coloring appears chalky, faded, abraded at seams, or has a vintage washed-out look, designate primary as Pigment Tie-Dye (#pigment_tie_dye). In all cases, set the alternate candidate as an invisible search tag (invisible_hashtags) so users can expand search across similar descriptions without polluting the primary classification.
example_negative: Never omit the alternative dye type from invisible search tags when tie-dye chemistry cannot be physically verified by lab test.
source_feedback: User Directive on Tie-Dye Ambiguity & Search Expansion

rule_title: Sample Stage is NOT Garment Type
condition_trigger: Spec sheet or label specifies sample stage codes such as 復辦, 大辦, 洗水辦, 產前辦, or 齊色辦.
rule_instruction: FORBIDDEN: Do not record sample development stages (e.g. 復辦/Repeat Sample, 大辦/Production Sample, 洗水辦/Washed Sample) as the garment_type. Garment type must be the actual silhouette (e.g. Polo Shirt, T-Shirt, Pullover). Record sample stage in remark_memo.
example_positive: Garment Type: Short-Sleeve Polo Shirt; Remark: 大辦 (Production Sample)

rule_instruction: Always expand HB to Hugo Boss.

rule_title: Hugo Boss Permanent Brand Architecture (HUGO vs BOSS)
condition_trigger: Tag mentions 'HB', 'Hugo Boss', 'BOSS', or 'HUGO' (and division lines Black, Orange, Green)
rule_instruction: Hugo Boss restructured into two distinct brand pillars: 'HUGO' and 'BOSS'. They operate separate standalone retail stores, differing design languages, and distinct target demographics (HUGO: Gen Z / progressive streetwear / red branding; BOSS: contemporary luxury / modern tailoring / camel-black-white branding, with lines BOSS Black, BOSS Orange, BOSS Green). This corporate restructuring is permanent, not a temporal line.
example_positive: HB -> HUGO BOSS / Boss Green Men (BGM)
source_feedback: User Merchandising Context: Hugo Boss restructured into two distinct brand pillars: 'HUGO' and 'BOSS'. They have separate retail stores, differing design languages, and distinct target demographics. This is a permanent brand architecture, not a temporal line.
